cropPriceNote: Minneapolis terminal bids — your local elevator will be lower
outlook: Grains closed lower Tuesday on fund and technical selling: December corn fell 5¾ cents to $4.42½ (about a four-month low), January soybeans lost 2¾ cents to $12.14, December Chicago wheat dropped 6¾ cents to $5.99¾ and December Minneapolis spring wheat settled 6¼ cents lower at $6.19½. Wheat was pressured by planned Russia–Ukraine–U.S. talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11, which could ease Black Sea shipping risks, and fresh corn sales to Mexico (315,000 tonnes) and South Korea (136,000 tonnes) plus 134,000 tonnes of soybeans to unknown destinations did little to lift prices. In Wednesday morning trade corn was near unchanged, Chicago wheat was up about 4 cents, January soybeans were down about 9 cents and January canola was down about C$10. Traders are watching the late U.S. harvest, South American planting and next Tuesday's USDA WASDE report.
